title: Quick check: Updating Objects in State

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Updating Objects in State”?
options: The concept allows application code to mutate React-managed DOM and state directly.
Copying existing objects should use state setters and immutable next values so React can update the UI predictably.
The concept removes the need to consider error states or accessibility.
The browser will infer all application behavior even if inputs and state are contradictory.
questions.answer_key: Copying existing objects should use state setters and immutable next values so React can update the UI predictably.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Updating Objects in State: Copying existing objects should use state setters and immutable next values so React can update the UI predictably.

questions.prompt: Which practice is most reliable when applying Copying existing objects?
options: Use functional updates when the new value depends on previous state, and do not mutate objects or arrays.
Skip validation because a successful render proves that the application is correct.
Store duplicate copies of every value so each component can change it independently.
Optimize by adding every available Hook without measuring the result.
questions.answer_key: Use functional updates when the new value depends on previous state, and do not mutate objects or arrays.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Updating Objects in State: Use functional updates when the new value depends on previous state, and do not mutate objects or arrays.

questions.prompt: What should you verify before considering “Updating Objects in State” complete?
options: Check only whether the file exists; syntax and runtime behavior do not matter.
Assume a client-side check proves that a remote service accepted the change.
Rely only on a screenshot of the happy path and never repeat the test.
Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
questions.answer_key: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Updating Objects in State: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
